title: [Lean] Decode compact bytes and recover the L450 source operator
body:
## Total compact bytes to the L450 source operator

Author-checked contextual κ = 836330098538459/500000000000000000 = 0.001672660197076918, at selected source revision 299eb8effe080183313757ac36e76c1b98ed9fae. The generic results do not use or change κ; this is not the full multiplication theorem.

Five unchanged, independently accepted Lean 4.21.0 sources add:
- A total decimal valuation left inverse for Nat.repr.
- Strict compact Nat-array and bounded-column decoding, with success iff exact canonical bytes.
- Actual decoded columns feeding unchanged restricted provider recovery, deriving the independent operator and both inverse laws.
- Closed decoder/recovery applications to the previously bound original 907-byte L450 literal and its old source operator.

All 14 probes and ten complete types are recorded; no new selected scalar census or large literal decision was run. The package reuses 98 immutable public prerequisites and adds 24,208 source bytes. Historical preparation labels are retained with source-hash-matched acceptance and private publication readiness evidence.

The new total path has no logical Json.parse premise. It does not prove the old opaque parser equation, whole-file field identity, authenticated artifact origin, compiler/runtime extern refinement, complex phases, physical execution or costs. Prospective bounded reproduction and the exact artifact boundary are documented. No compilation or archive replay occurred during packaging.

## Exact adoption

Publication parent: 0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2. The five selected-result, assembly, selected-source and emitter blobs match the previously checked context exactly; contextual kappa is unchanged. No accepted proof was rerun for this adoption.
